nodes.label: Per-tenant customizable customer-facing email templates (template_key registry)
email_templates table (tenant_id + template_key unique registry of subject/body)
Tenant-isolation RLS convention: every row gated on tenant_id = get_user_tenant_id()
Idempotent reconciliation of a live table whose columns drifted from the code (body/name/category to template_content/template_name/template_key)
Rationale: every ALTER wrapped in an information_schema existence check because the deployed table shape was unknown/partially migrated
Destructive gotcha: silently DELETEs duplicate (tenant_id, template_key) rows to make the unique constraint addable
Legacy email_templates columns retained but made nullable so new code never has to write them
Catalog-driven policy reset: loop pg_policies and DROP every policy on the table before recreating
Canonical tenant-isolation shape: one FOR ALL policy TO authenticated with get_user_tenant_id() OR is_super_admin()
Rationale: four RLS rewrites in one day because the first three used per-verb policies with no super-admin bypass ('match pattern from other tables')
One-off purge of orphaned financial rows plus retrofit of real FK constraints on rentals/payments/fines/ledger_entries
Rationale: dangling customer_id/vehicle_id references made PostgREST embedded joins return 400 errors in the apps
Financial teardown order: ledger_entries and payment_applications must die before payments, payments before rentals
Deliberate FK asymmetry: customer deletion CASCADEs away money rows, vehicle deletion only SET NULLs them so financial history survives fleet churn
_orphaned_data_audit table (forensic log of purged orphans, documented as droppable after verification)
rentals table (core rental agreement row)
payments table (money received against a rental)
ledger_entries table (double-entry style ledger referencing rentals AND payments)
payment_applications table (allocation of a payment to charges)
fines table (penalty charges; no rental_id column)
pnl_entries table (per-vehicle profit and loss entries)
insurance_policies table (customer insurance cover records)
customers table (renter identity, tenant-scoped)
vehicles table (fleet inventory and availability status)
AI identity verification (OCR + face match) as a swappable alternative to the Veriff provider
QR desktop-to-mobile verification handoff (qr_session_token + expiry, partial index for token lookup)
identity_verifications table (per-customer ID check, Veriff or AI, with QR mobile session)
Free-text service-type classification on vehicle maintenance records
service_records table (vehicle maintenance history)
Compliance audit trail of who did what to which entity, per tenant
audit_logs table (tenant_id, actor_id, action, entity_type/id, JSONB details)
Gotcha: audit_logs INSERT policy is WITH CHECK (true) plus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so any caller can forge a row for any tenant while even the table owner is subject to RLS
Ordering anomaly: the audit_logs policy migration is timestamped 20260104120000, one hour BEFORE the CREATE TABLE migration 20260104130000 that defines the table
app_users table (portal staff identity, links auth.uid to tenant and role)
Optional 17-character VIN identifier on fleet vehicles
Auto-link an ID verification started anonymously during booking to the customer record created later, keyed on email + tenant
Partial index scoped to WHERE customer_email IS NOT NULL AND customer_id IS NULL so only still-unlinked verifications are indexed
Rental payment mode: 'auto' means immediate capture, 'manual' means a pre-authorisation hold captured later
Rental status is derived, not stored: approval_status (pending/approved/rejected) crossed with payment_status (pending/fulfilled/failed/refunded)
Backfill: legacy Active and Closed rentals are assumed approved+fulfilled; Cancelled rentals are deliberately left as pending because the reason is unknowable
Free-text cancellation reason taxonomy (rejected_insurance, rejected_id, customer_requested, early_termination, breach_of_contract) kept uncontrained by CHECK
Cross-tenant fraud blacklist: an email blocked by enough independent tenants becomes globally blocked
global_blacklist table (email-unique, platform-wide, deliberately NOT tenant-scoped)
blocked_identities table (per-tenant block list by identity_type/identity_number; source of truth for the global rollup)
v_global_blacklist_details view (global entry joined to the tenants that blocked it and their stated reasons)
Three-tenant promotion threshold, and symmetric demotion: if active blocks drop below 3 the global row is DELETEd, so the blacklist is recomputed not accumulated

Anonymous SELECT on global_blacklist granted on purpose so the unauthenticated booking flow can screen an email before signup; no anon write path exists (mutations only via SECURITY DEFINER functions)
Public read surface for the booking sites: anon may read published CMS pages, their sections, and active tenants
Rationale: policies already existed on cms_pages/cms_page_sections/tenants but RLS was never ENABLEd, so none of them were being enforced
Table-level GRANT SELECT on tenants to anon — the grant that multi-tenant subdomain routing and branding depend on for unauthenticated visitors
cms_pages table (per-tenant editable marketing/booking-site pages, slug + status)
cms_page_sections table (content blocks belonging to a cms_page; visibility inherited from the parent page)
cms_page_versions table (CMS revision history, tenant-scoped)
tenants table (rental operator; root of every tenant-isolation predicate)
delete_rental_cascade: hand-written SECURITY DEFINER teardown of a rental and every dependent row, ending by releasing the vehicle back to Available
Rationale: ledger_entries.payment_id references payments.id, so ledger_entries must be deleted BEFORE payments — arbitrary order raises fk_ledger_entries_payment_id violations
Deleting an Active rental frees its vehicle by setting vehicles.status = 'Available' — availability is a denormalised field the teardown must maintain
Handover photos hang off rental_key_handovers via handover_id, not rental_id, so they need a subquery hop during teardown

Correction: fines and reminders have no rental_id at all (reminders keys on object_type/object_id) — the cascade targets reminder_events instead; the rental_protection_selections undefined_table guard is also dropped
Defensive EXCEPTION WHEN undefined_table guard so the function survives environments where rental_protection_selections was never created
invoices table (rental-linked invoice rows)
reminder_events table (per-rental reminder dispatch events; the rental-linked half of the reminder system)
reminders table (polymorphic object_type/object_id reminders, NOT rental-keyed)
rental_key_handovers table (key handover event per rental, incl. lockbox/in-person delivery)
rental_handover_photos table (condition photos, keyed by handover_id)
rental_insurance_verifications table (insurance check outcome tied to a rental)
rental_protection_selections table (optional protection/waiver add-ons; may not exist in every environment)
customer_documents table (uploaded IDs, insurance certificates and other proofs; optionally rental-linked)
Backfill of the eight default CMS pages (home, about, contact, fleet, reviews, promotions, terms, privacy) for tenants created before the auto-seed trigger existed
Super-admin bypass retrofitted onto every cms_pages / cms_page_sections / cms_page_versions policy so the admin app can edit any tenant's content
tenant_id IS NULL means a platform-global CMS page; it is readable AND updatable by every authenticated user, unlike INSERT/DELETE which require an owning tenant or super admin
Section-level access is never stored: cms_page_sections policies re-derive it with an EXISTS lookup on the parent cms_pages row
Double-upload prevention for insurance certificates: dedupe existing rows keeping the oldest, then enforce uniqueness at the database
Two mutually exclusive partial unique indexes because an insurance doc uploaded during booking has no rental yet: one keyed on rental_id, one on customer_id WHERE rental_id IS NULL
AI insurance-document decisioning with banded thresholds: auto_approved at 85%+, auto_rejected below 60%, pending_review in between, plus manual override states
Fraud risk scoring 0..1 on insurance documents (expired dates, inconsistent data, suspicious patterns) with a partial index over the >= 0.5 monitoring band
review_reasons text[] records WHY a document was routed to a human, so the manual-review queue is explainable
Anon UPDATE policy so the phone-side verification page can push verification_step / upload_progress and the desktop tab watches it live

Gotcha: the anon UPDATE policy is scoped only by status != 'completed' — it names no session token, tenant or row owner, so any anon caller can mutate any in-progress verification; 'completed' is the only immutability boundary

hyperedges.label: Six same-day migrations converging one drifted email_templates table onto the repo's canonical schema and RLS shape
The rental financial teardown chain (payment_applications, ledger_entries, payments, rentals, vehicle release) rediscovered by both the orphan cleanup and three delete_rental_cascade revisions

Verification artefacts created before a customer/rental row exists: QR mobile handoff, anon progress writes, email auto-linking, and pre-rental document dedupe all key off nullable customer_id/rental_id
